facts.content: Patient reports a 3-day history of a severe headache that she describes as 'crazy' and worse today.
The headache pain is mostly around the right eye but also generalized.
facts.source_text: Pain mostly around right eye, also generalized

facts.content: The headache is described as a dull ache that is occasionally sharper with gradual onset.
facts.source_text: Dull ache, occasionally sharper; gradual onset

facts.content: The headache has been persistent over three days and fluctuates in intensity with exacerbations.
facts.source_text: Persistent, fluctuates in intensity (baseline, with exacerbations);

facts.content: The patient rates the current headache intensity as 8 out of 10.
The headache is worsened after sleep.
Ibuprofen taken three times daily for the past two days has been ineffective for the headache.
The patient reports photophobia with eye pain in bright light.
facts.source_text: Photophobia; eye pain with bright light

facts.content: The patient denies vision loss or blurring but reports occasional 'shooting lights'.
facts.source_text: No vision loss/blurring; reports occasional “shooting lights”

facts.content: The headache is associated with mild nausea and no vomiting.
The patient denies fever, neck stiffness, rash, speech difficulty, and limb weakness.
facts.source_text: No fever, neck stiffness, rash, speech difficulty, limb weakness

facts.content: The patient reports difficulty concentrating due to the headache and has taken days off work.
facts.source_text: Concentration difficulty; took days off work

facts.content: The patient has a history of similar mild headaches in the past that were responsive to ibuprofen.
facts.source_text: Hx: Similar mild HA in past, responsive to ibuprofen

facts.content: The patient is concerned that this could be a migraine and has researched genetics and triggers.
facts.source_text: Concerned about possible migraine; researched genetics and triggers

facts.content: The patient denies any past medical history.
The patient reports taking no regular medications.
The patient has taken ibuprofen three times daily over the past two days for the headache.
The patient reports no known drug allergies.
There is a family history of migraine in the patient's mother and sister.
The patient lives with three housemates.
The patient works in IT and reports that screen use aggravates the headache.
facts.source_text: Works in IT; screen use aggravates HA;

facts.content: The patient wears glasses and has not had a recent eye check.
The patient is a social smoker.
The patient drinks alcohol socially.
The patient reports recent work stress but denies severe anxiety.
facts.source_text: Recent work stress; denies severe anxiety

facts.content: Clinician assessment is acute severe headache with possible migraine.
The acute severe headache has been present for 3 days, is periorbital and right-sided, associated with photophobia and nausea, with a family history of migraine and poor response to ibuprofen.
facts.source_text: 3 days, periorbital/right-sided, photophobia, N, family hx migraine, ibuprofen ineffective

facts.content: The correct dosing of ibuprofen up to 2 tablets three times daily was discussed with the patient.
facts.source_text: Discussed correct dosing of ibuprofen (up to 2 tab TID)

facts.content: The patient was offered a prescription for naproxen and/or codeine.
facts.source_text: Offered Rx for naproxen and/or codeine;

facts.content: Paracetamol was discussed as an additional option for headache management.
The patient was advised to keep a headache diary to track frequency and triggers.
facts.source_text: Advise headache diary to track frequency/triggers

facts.content: Follow-up was recommended in 1 to 2 weeks with consideration of migraine prophylaxis if headaches are recurrent.
facts.source_text: F/U in 1–2 wks; consider migraine prophylaxis if recurrent

facts.content: The patient was educated about warning signs such as vision changes, neurological deficits, and systemic symptoms and instructed to seek urgent care if these occur.
facts.source_text: Educated re: warning signs (vision changes, neuro deficits, systemic sx)—to seek URGENT care if present

facts.content: The patient was advised to have an eye test if eye strain persists.
facts.source_text: Suggested eye test if eye strain persists

facts.content: The patient is to follow up in 1 to 2 weeks.
No physical examination or vital signs were documented.
The patient reports photophobia.
The patient reports occasional 'shooting lights' in her vision.
The patient reports mild nausea without vomiting.
The patient denies fever, neck stiffness, rash, speech difficulty, and limb weakness.
facts.source_text: No fever, neck stiffness, rash, speech difficulty, limb weakness
